commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Offload model runner construction buffers on sleep
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59158. Part of RFC #59055.

#59158 builds the KV-cache initialization state inside the `runtime` cuMem pool, so sleep backs it up to CPU and restores it on wake. Buffers that the model runner allocates in its constructor are still allocated outside every pool, so they stay on the GPU while asleep. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash with MTP, the drafter's `hidden_states` buffer (`spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py`) is 512 MiB/GPU.

The earlier revision of #59158 built the model runner inside the `runtime` pool too; that part was dropped before merge. This PR brings it back:

- `Worker` builds the model runner inside the `runtime` pool.
- The check that the allocator is unused when the `weights` pool is entered is removed. The runner now enters the `runtime` pool first, so the check would fire whenever its constructor allocates (MTP, DSpark). It guarded two engines sharing one `CuMemAllocator` in a process, which V1 rules out by default because the engine core runs in its own process.

## Test Plan

- `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep` in `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` (from #59158) now allocates its state while `Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner` builds the runner, instead of under the `runtime` pool directly. It passed on main before; now it fails there (`{'kv_cache'} == {'kv_cache', 'runtime'}`) and passes with this change. Its other checks (nested `kv_cache` tag, offload, restore by the first selective wake) are unchanged.
- `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`, with and without this change.
- GB300, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 + EP4 with MTP, level-1 sleep: memory while asleep, with and without `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, and outputs after wake compared with the awake run.

## Test Result

At c2e07c4deb (main c9e4cb2b79), GB200:
- `test_runtime_state_survives_sleep` fails on main and passes here; `test_cumem.py` 22 passed; `test_gpu_worker.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` + `test_kv_cache_allocation_scope.py` 64 passed.
- `test_sleep_mode.py` 16 passed, 1 skipped, on Model Runner V2 (default) and on V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`).
- With a speculator, so the runner allocates while it is built: `test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization_survives_sleep_and_reload` (Qwen3.5 MTP, V2) passed.

Earlier results, before the check was dropped:

- `test_cumem.py`: 16 passed with this change vs 14 on main; the 7 failures are the same on both sides (models not in the offline cache). `test_gpu_worker.py` + `test_sleep_mode_backend.py`: 29 passed on both.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, memory per GPU while asleep:

| | main (+ graph pool released) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| sleep mode | 8633 MiB | 8121 MiB (−512) |
| + `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` | 6451 MiB | 5939 MiB (−512) |

- The `runtime` tag grows from 4704 to 5218 MiB. Outputs after two wakes are identical to the awake run, and wake time is unchanged.
- Not yet covered: GSM8K.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Move model inspection RPC out of LLM.__repr__
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep `LLM.__repr__` local so debugger variable inspection does not implicitly issue blocking worker RPCs. Move the existing model hierarchy inspection and cache into an explicit `LLM.get_model_inspection()` method.

## Claims

- `repr(llm)` and `print(llm)` return a local summary such as `LLM(model='Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B')` without querying workers.
- The full model hierarchy remains available through `llm.get_model_inspection()`, with the existing first-call caching behavior.
- Add an `LLM` regression test and document the explicit inspection API in the offline inference guide.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_collective_rpc.py::test_model_inspection_requires_explicit_call
```

Result from the submitter's latest local run: **1 passed, 15 warnings in 26.72s** (Python 3.12.13), using `vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`.

The test constructs a real `LLM` with a tiny Llama checkpoint, checks the local representation, and verifies that explicit inspection returns the model hierarchy. It covers the public API behavior; the VS Code thread-blocking scenario is not automated by this test. A before-fix run of the regression test remains to be recorded.

Additional validation: the following pre-commit run passed all applicable hooks, including Ruff, Markdown lint, mypy, and test-to-CI wiring checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/llm.py \
  tests/entrypoints/llm/test_collective_rpc.py \
  docs/serving/offline_inference.md
```

Model evaluations are not applicable: this change affects object display and explicit inspection, without changing model execution, generation, or serving behavior.

## Details

VS Code/debugpy can call `repr()` automatically when displaying variables. Previously, the first such call on an `LLM` invoked `self.llm_engine.collective_rpc("get_model_inspection")`. If completing that RPC depends on threads or workers that are paused or blocked during debugging, variable inspection can stall waiting for the response. Caching only helps after the first successful call.

[Python's data model documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/reference/datamodel.html#object.__repr__) describes `__repr__` as commonly used for debugging. [debugpy maintainers explain](https://github.com/microsoft/debugpy/issues/952) that the debugger invokes `repr()` for unfamiliar types, and that a representation blocked in native I/O cannot reliably be interrupted with a Python exception. These are the reasons for keeping `LLM.__repr__` local; 

Users who need the hierarchy previously shown by `print(llm)` can now request it explicitly:

```python
print(llm.get_model_inspection())
```

The first explicit call still performs synchronous worker RPC and may block. Subsequent calls return the cached result. The existing selection of the first worker's result and local-summary fallback for an empty result are preserved.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for `get_model_inspection`, `repr in:title`, `repr debugger`, `repr blocking`, and `61366 in:body`. Related PRs [#61414](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61414) and [#61613](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61613) address non-PyTorch model inspection errors and retain the RPC in `__repr__`. This PR addresses implicit blocking during debugger variable inspection; no open PR implementing that fix was found in those searches.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and its PR description.

This is my first contribution to vLLM. Feedback on the approach and tests is welcome, and I’m happy to address any review comments.

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal][Bugfix] Fix Step3-VL encoder output aliasing and guard shared CUDA graph capture buffers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #65084, which shares encoder CUDA graph capture buffers across token budgets. Sharing introduced two issues, and this PR fixes both:

1. Step3-VL returns views of the graph output, which a later replay overwrites.
2. The model protocol was tightened without saying so: buffers written only at capture time can be overwritten by other budgets.

## Claims

- **Step3-VL embeddings no longer get overwritten.** A no-patch image's embedding was a view of the `global` graph output, even with `clone=True`. A later replay in the same `execute()` overwrote it. Before #65084 this needed two batches on the *same* budget; with sharing, any budget on the path does it. Fix: honor `clone`.
- **Capture-time-only buffers are guarded.**
  - Before: 0-dim buffers were shared wholesale, so after capture every budget's graph saw the smallest budget's value. A shared buffer that replay did not refill silently kept another budget's contents.
  - After: 0-dim buffers stay per budget. These scalars cost no memory, so nothing is lost. Replay raises if it omits a buffer that smaller budgets view.
  - The constraints are documented: replay must refill shared buffers, `padding_logics` must write the whole destination, and `postprocess_encoder_output(clone=True)` must not alias its outputs.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py`): 118 passed.

| Test | Covers | Fails without the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_step3_vl_postprocess_clones_global_only_item` (new) | Step3-VL honors `clone=True` | ✔ |
| `test_replay_without_shared_buffer_raises` (new) | Replay guard | ✔ |
| `test_scalar_buffers_keep_own_value` (was `test_scalar_buffers_are_shared`) | Each budget's graph keeps its own scalar | ✔ |

**End-to-end on MI355X** (Model Runner V2, default budgets). A 3-image prompt with `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch=2` splits one `execute()` into several batches. Each returned embedding is compared with the same image encoded alone (relative L2; bf16 noise is ≤ 0.05).

| Model | Corrupted embeddings, before → after | Capture buffers, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| Step3-VL-10B | **5/11 → 0/11** (max rel. error 0.62 → 0.04) | 430.1 → 430.1 MiB |
| Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct | 0/11 → 0/11 | 488.0 → 488.0 MiB |
| Gemma4-E2B-it | 0/11 → 0/11 | 344.1 → 344.1 MiB |
| MiniMax-M3 (TP2, `mm_encoder_tp_mode=data`) | — → 0/11; guard not triggered | — → 554.0 MiB |

## Details

- **Why main is safe today.** The only capture-time-only key in-tree is the CPU `max_seqlen`. ViT attention reads it with `.item()` at capture, so later overwrites never reach a graph. The guard and the docs keep future or out-of-tree models from silently depending on this.
- **Why the fix is in Step3-VL, not the manager.** Every other `postprocess_encoder_output` already returns fresh tensors. Cloning in the manager would add a full copy for all of them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pad Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram inputs for piecewise CUDA graph replays
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61486

The Qwen4Exp AMD backend computes PLE n-gram ids inside PIECEWISE CUDA graph pieces, where the request search keeps the count the piece was captured with, but `Qwen4ExpModelState` only refreshed the live batch's rows of `query_start_loc` and
`ngram_context`. Replays read a stale tail, hashed the wrong n-gram and made the answer depend on what the server had served before. This pads both buffers.

## Claims

- PLE n-gram inputs no longer depend on server history: 0/300 short prompts change their answer after a 16-way burst, versus 77/300 before.
- Bit-identical replays: the max first-token logprob delta after the burst is 0.0000, versus 0.72 before.
- Eager and FULL-graph steps are unaffected: there `num_reqs_padded == num_reqs`, so the refreshed range already covers what the graph reads.


## Validation

vllm serving command:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --enable-prefix-caching --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

Using the reproducible script provided, 300 prompts served sequentially and greedily, the same prompts again as a control, a 16-way concurrent burst, then the same prompts again. Only the server state accumulated in between differs. 

---

<details>
<summary>Reproducer script (300-prompt history test)</summary>

```python
"""300-prompt history test for issue 61486.

Run against the server above. Each prompt is generated three times, and the first
16 are reused as the burst; only the server state accumulated in between differs.
Expected: the control reports 0 changed prompts, and the effect reports 0 with
the fix (about 25-30% without it).
"""
import json
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from datasets import load_dataset

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8"


def post(path, payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600).read())


def gen(ids, max_tokens=8):
    out = post(
        "/v1/completions",
        {"model": MODEL, "prompt": ids, "max_tokens": max_tokens,
         "temperature": 0.0, "logprobs": 1},
    )
    lp = out["choices"][0]["logprobs"]
    return {"tokens": lp["tokens"], "logprob0": lp["token_logprobs"][0]}


def run_set(prompts):
    return [gen(ids) for ids in prompts]  # sequential, fixed order


questions = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test")["question"][:300]
prompts = [
    post("/tokenize", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": q})["tokens"] for q in questions
]

first = run_set(prompts)
again = run_set(prompts)  # control: nothing changed in between
with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:  # concurrent traffic, then repeat
    list(ex.map(lambda ids: gen(ids, 24), prompts[:16]))
after = run_set(prompts)

for name, a, b in (("control", first, again), ("effect ", first, after)):
    changed = sum(x["tokens"] != y["tokens"] for x, y in zip(a, b))
    delta = max(abs(x["logprob0"] - y["logprob0"]) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    print(f"{name}: {changed}/{len(a)} prompts changed, max |dlogprob0| = {delta:.4f}")
```

</details>

---

| suite | main | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| answers changed, first pass vs after burst (n=300) | 77/300 = 25.7% (95% CI 20.8-31.0) | **0/300** (95% CI 0-1.2) |
| max first-token logprob delta after the burst | 0.72 | **0.0000** |
| control, same prompts twice, no burst | 0/300 | 0/300 |


GSM8k: 

```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

```

result:

| suite | this fix |
|---|---|
| lm-eval gsm8k 25-shot (1319) | 0.9765 +- 0.0042 |

Pytest: 
```
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py  ->  15 passed
same file, fix reverted  ->  test_qwen4_exp_model_state_pads_replayed_request_range[amd] fails
```

## Details

PIECEWISE descriptors carry `num_reqs=None`, so the runner does not pad the request axis, while the captured piece uses `num_reqs = min(piece_tokens, max_num_seqs)`. `qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_ids` is not a splitting op and sizes its search from
`query_start_loc.numel() - 1`, so it keeps the capture-time count and reads rows this step never wrote. For a 24-token batch, `prepare_inputs` refreshed `query_start_loc[0:2]` while the piece reads `query_start_loc[0:25]`.

* Added a new test, covering both NVIDIA and AMD platform: buffers are non-decreasing, unused capacity cannot capture real tokens, a search over the captured request range resolves every real token to its own request (request-padded and unpadded cases), rows the batch does not own are sentinels, and the capture-time dummy inputs follow the same convention.

Each buffer is handed over as the smallest view the kernel needs: `query_start_loc` as the live prefix, because the kernel derives its request count from the view length, and `ngram_context` as the whole buffer, because it indexes rows by request, so every
reachable row must be valid. Passing the full buffers, as the NVIDIA copy does, also fixes this, but makes every eager and FULL step search `max_num_reqs + 1` boundaries instead of the live count. Therefore preferring this over the NVIDIA fixes.

Additional info: steps whose padded token count exceeds the largest captured piece (512 here) run eager and were never affected, so long and few-shot prompts show no difference; short prompts, chunked prefill and prefix-cache continuations are the exposed cases. The two model states remain separate per-backend copies; I can unify them in a follow-up PR if preferred.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Use the upstream config for MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Deletes the vendored `MossTranscribeDiarizeConfig` and loads MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize through the upstream class, keeping the Whisper encoder config of original checkpoints. Prerequisite for #65735, which replaces #62398. Same treatment as #66097 for Qwen3-ASR.

## Claims

- Transformers-format checkpoints (`hf-audio/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize-HF`) get the upstream config instead of the vendored one, so #65735 no longer needs a special case to serve them with `--model-impl transformers`.
- No change in what vLLM builds or outputs for `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize` on Transformers >= 5.20.

## Validation

| Checkpoint | Model dump diffs | Output, before vs after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize` | 0 | Identical (`diarized_json`, 14 segments on 41 s of audio) |

Run on Transformers 5.23.0.dev0 and one B200 GPU, with `--trust-remote-code`. Config loading was also checked on the 5.16.1 floor.

```bash
S=.agents/skills/transformers-upgrade/scripts
PYTHONPATH=<base> python $S/dump_model.py before.jsonl OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python $S/dump_model.py after.jsonl OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize
python $S/diff_dumps.py before.jsonl after.jsonl
pytest tests/transformers_utils tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k MossTranscribe
```

149 passed. The `-k MossTranscribe` tests skip because the checkpoint is marked unavailable online, so the API comparison above is the native coverage.

## Details

- The upstream class exists from Transformers 5.20. Below that (floor 5.16.1), the checkpoint's remote config is used, so the config now needs `--trust-remote-code` too. The test registry already sets it.
- Without `--trust-remote-code`, the original checkpoint fails natively both before (`KeyError: 'padding_mask'`) and after (`adaptor_input_dim` has no setter, as it is a property upstream) on >= 5.20.
- `hf-audio/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize-HF` does not load on the native class before or after, so it needs `--model-impl transformers` (#65735).

commits.pr_title: [XPU][UT] Preserve RoPE buffer dtype for HF reference in the privacy-filter model test on XPU
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the privacy-filter token-classification test on XPU by preserving the HFrunner model’s original FP32 RoPE frequency buffers (eg, inv_freq) instead of downcasting them to BF16. This change aligns the buffer dtype of hfrunner with vllmrunner.

Following [#64705](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64705), this PR triaged the root cause and resolved it.

## Claims

-  The ROPE buffer dtype of `hfrunner` and `vllmrunner` are bf16 and fp32, respectively. This leads to numerical diff during model inference and make this ut fail with the fifth prompt on XPU.
- This PR preserves the buffer dtype as fp32 only for this case and only on XPU.
- On Cuda, the fifth prompt (the one failed on XPU) also shows larger output diff with RoPE buffer downcasting (0.0508 with bf16, 0.0354 with fp32). This diff still remains within the tolerance so the ut passed on cuda.

## Validation
to reproduce: need to fix a workspace crash issue with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65318 and then run ut
```
pytest -s -v tests/models/language/pooling/test_token_classification.py::test_openai_privacy_filter
```

result before this PR:
```
E           AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E           
E           Mismatched elements: 2 / 429 (0.5%)
E           Greatest absolute difference: 0.13447123765945435 at index (12, 7) (up to 0.1 allowed)
E           Greatest relative difference: 0.35410743951797485 at index (12, 0) (up to 0.01 allowed)

tests/models/language/pooling/test_token_classification.py:196: AssertionError
```

result after this PR: passed.

## Details

### Some references
- HfRunner’s whole-model BF16 conversion also downcasts the inv_freq buffer to BF16: [tests/conftest.py#L531-L535](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd1effa2e7d204b22527f14739734751f38ed737/tests/conftest.py#L531-L535).

- vLLM explicitly initializes RoPE with FP32, computes inv_freq in FP32, and uses it to generate the cos/sin cache: [gpt_oss.py#L111-L117](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd1effa2e7d204b22527f14739734751f38ed737/vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py#L111-L117) → [yarn_scaling_rope.py#L51-L74](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd1effa2e7d204b22527f14739734751f38ed737/vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn_scaling_rope.py#L51-L74) → [yarn_scaling_rope.py#L81](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd1effa2e7d204b22527f14739734751f38ed737/vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/yarn_scaling_rope.py#L81).

### More exp on XPU about inv_freq bf16 vs fp32
- Frequency precision: Downcasting changes 31 of the 32 frequencies. eg, 0.6890442967414856 (FP32) -> 0.6875 (BF16).
- First-layer attention output: 3/7 prompts fail assert_close(atol=0.1, rtol=0.01).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Validate CLI stochastic rounding against the platform
commits.pr_body:
- `arg_utils.py`: re-run `MambaConfig.__post_init__()` after the CLI Mamba overrides, instead of only `validate_ssu_algorithm()`.
- `test_arg_utils.py`: regression test that `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` on a non-CUDA platform fails at config time with the platform error.

`MambaConfig.__post_init__` rejects Mamba cache stochastic rounding on non-CUDA platforms and, for the Triton backend, on anything other than SM100, because the Triton kernels use the PTX `cvt.rs.f16x2.f32` instruction. `EngineArgs.create_engine_config` copies the default `MambaConfig` (where the flag is off) and only then sets `enable_stochastic_rounding` from the CLI, so those checks never ran for the CLI flag and only `validate_ssu_algorithm()` was called again. On MI355 a Nemotron-3-Super ReplaySSM server with `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` got through config and died in warmup with `RuntimeError: LLD failed to link hsaco ... ld.lld: error: target emulation unknown`. With this change the same command fails at config time with the intended "only supported on NVIDIA CUDA platforms" error. `__post_init__` only does validation, so running it again is safe and also keeps future checks there in sync with the CLI path.

## Overview Encoder (ViT) CUDA graphs only help while eager is bound by host launch time. On main, graphs are captured up to `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384 by default), and a batch is greedily split into several padded replays, so large batches often run slower as graphs than eagerly. This PR applies one rule to every model, in the style of the LLM's CUDA graphs: - **One replay per batch.** A batch replays the smallest budget that holds it; anything else runs as one eager forward. - **A finer budget grid up to one global maximum.** The new `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (default 5120) works like the LLM's maximum capture size. The default balances graph memory against replay coverage using the GB200 measurements below; it is not a universal GPU-bound threshold. Larger batches run eagerly, with a known Gemma 4 trade-off documented below. `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` still overrides both. No model has its own setting. Follow-up: #66067 (stacked on this PR) moves the per-model encoder CUDA graph code that is copied across Qwen2/2.5/3-VL, GLM-4.1V and Cohere Compass into shared mixins, with no behavior change. **This PR builds on #65084** (shared capture buffers, by @Isotr0py), which is now merged; it is rebased onto it. All budget graphs share one set of input and output buffers sized for the largest budget, so the finer grid below costs no extra buffer memory. This PR's own changes: - [`fcba393f65`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65227/commits/fcba393f65): one replay per batch, budget grid, global maximum, largest item first, and eager-path fixes. - [`8bf9354b99`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65227/commits/8bf9354b99): GLM-4.1V rounds its capture size up like the other models. **This also fixes a crash on current main.** #65084's finer budgets (80, 96, ...) make GLM-4.1V's round-down capture too few rows, so with encoder CUDA graphs on (the default) a single 252x252 image stops the engine with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (324)` (GLM-4.1V-9B, GB200, default `limit_mm_per_prompt`; eager runs). With this PR the same requests run, with both video-enabled and image-only limits, and match eager within run-to-run noise (except the known 672x672 video-enabled case fixed by #65453). See Details. - The remaining commits document and validate `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget`. ## How dispatch changes `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute()` receives one encoder batch (all images or videos the scheduler sends to the encoder in one step) and returns one output per item. **Before (main).** A batch is greedily split into groups, and each group replays its own padded graph. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Encoder batch: N items"] --> B["Sort items, smallest first"] B --> C["Greedy packing into groups:
each group has at most max_batch_size items
and at most the largest budget in tokens (16384 by default);
a large item also starts a new group when running it
separately needs less total budget than merging it"] C --> D["Next group"] D --> E{"Smallest captured budget
that holds the group?"} E -- "found" --> F["Replay that graph
(input padded up to the budget)"] E -- "none: one item larger
than the largest budget" --> G["Eager forward of the group"] F --> H["Postprocess the group"] G --> H H -- "more groups" --> D H -- "done" --> I["Outputs in request order"] ``` A batch of K groups costs K replays, each padded to its budget. Graphs go up to 16384 tokens, where most encoders are already GPU-bound, so a large batch split into several padded replays is often slower than one eager forward. **After (this PR).** The whole batch replays at most one graph; anything that does not fit runs as one eager forward. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Encoder batch: N items"] --> B["Sort items, largest first"] B --> C{"N <= max_batch_size, and a captured budget
(at most encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget, 5120)
holds all tokens of the batch?"} C -- "yes" --> D["One replay of the smallest such graph"] C -- "no" --> E["One eager forward of the whole batch"] D --> F["Postprocess once"] E --> F F --> G["Outputs in request order"] ``` Models with several encoder paths (Step3-VL, DeepSeek-OCR) take this decision once per path. **Captured graphs (startup).** | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | Budgets | Quarter-octave steps up to 1024, then half-octave steps, up to the model's largest budget, usually `max_num_batched_tokens` (64, 80, 96, ..., 12288, 16384: 25 graphs) | Quarter-octave steps up to 1024, every 128 up to 2560, then 1/8-octave steps, up to `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (64, 80, 96, ..., 4608, 5120: 36 graphs). The same for every model | | Buffers | One set of buffers sized for the largest budget, shared by all graphs (#65084) | Unchanged; the largest budget is now 5120, so the shared buffers are smaller | | Fixed-size items (Step3-VL, DeepSeek-OCR) | Budgets are multiples of the item size, so up to 16 items fit exactly (#65084) | Unchanged | | User override | `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` | Unchanged; it also overrides the maximum | ## Claims - **Faster than current main** (which includes #65084): 1.07x–1.13x geomean encoder latency on 6 models with real weights, 1.10x–1.21x on batches above 2560 tokens. GLM-4.1V cannot be compared because current main crashes on it (see above); this PR fixes that. - **About 3x less graph memory than current main**, for example 4.99 → 1.79 GiB (MiniMax-M3) and 6.29 → 2.25 GiB (DeepSeek-V4.1), because graphs stop at 5120 tokens instead of 16384. - Against main before #65084 (the earlier measurements kept below): 1.03x–1.30x on 24 models. One known slower case: Gemma 4 batches of exactly 32 images run eagerly and are 9% slower than an exactly fitting graph (see "Choosing the maximum"). - **Simpler:** one global maximum instead of per-model tuning, and one replay per batch instead of greedy packing. This PR's own change is −10 lines outside tests and docs. - **Correct:** no batch on any model matches eager worse than on main, and the encoder CUDA graph test suite fails the same tests as on main. ## Validation All runs: GB200, BF16, default settings (no user budgets). ### Encoder latency and memory vs current main, real weights **Baseline** = main at `ebc97ad8d0` (includes #65084). **After PR** = this PR (`eebc7d0dcf`) on the same main. ## Details **Why a graph can lose.** Eager latency is roughly max(host launch time, GPU time). A replay costs the GPU time of its whole captured shape, padding included. Once eager is GPU-bound there is no launch time left to save, so padding and extra replays are pure cost. Main captures up to 16384 tokens and splits a batch into several padded replays. **Why one global maximum and not per-model tuning.** An earlier revision of this PR capped some models at 2560 and left others uncapped, based on per-model measurements. That needed a decision for every model and for every subclass that inherits one, so it is not maintainable. The measurements above support 5120 as a common memory/performance compromise, with the documented Gemma 4 32-image regression. Graph memory is a little higher than with per-model caps (MiniMax-M3 1.79 vs 1.01 GiB), and speed is within about 1–2%. **GLM-4.1V capture size (`8bf9354b99`).** GLM-4.1V sized each dummy capture item as `budget // max_batch_size`, while the other models round up. With the old power-of-2 budgets this was exact. The finer grid has budgets such as 96 with `max_batch_size` 64: one 96-token image needs 384 patch rows, but the graph captured 64 × 1 × 4 = 256, so replay fails in `_copy_padded_buffer` ("size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (384)"). Found on GLM-4.1V-9B with a single 96-token image. Since #65084 merged on its own, main has the finer budgets without this fix and crashes the same way (re-checked end to end on main `ebc97ad8d0`: a 252x252 image fails with 256 vs 324 rows; eager and main plus this commit run). After the fix, all 82 GLM-4.1V batches and all 34 GLM-5.3-Flash batches (which inherits the code) run and match eager as on main. **Eager paths.** Batches above the maximum now take each model's `encoder_eager_forward`, which main rarely used. Three were fixed: - **DeepSeek-V4.1:** ran one forward per image, which is 2–3x slower than main's graphs on large batches. It now runs all images as one varlen batch through the same forward as the graph. - **Ernie-4.5-VL:** ran the resampler twice and crashed (`shape '[-1, 10240]' is invalid`). - **DeepSeek-VL2:** had no `encoder_eager_forward` and returned `None`. **Trade-offs and limitations.** - **More graphs:** 36 instead of 9. Buffers are shared, so memory still drops. Capture takes 0–3 s longer, except GLM-4.1V (8.8 → 15.8 s). - **Other GPUs:** only GB200 was measured; no AMD hardware was available. If eager becomes GPU-bound later on another GPU, `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` can be raised. - **Video frame capacity (fixed by #60112):** a graph holds `min(max_batch_size * max_frames_per_video, token_budget)` frames. With the default video limit, `max_frames_per_video` is 1, so a single long low-resolution video (e.g. 130 frames at 112x112 on Qwen2.5-VL) overflows `cu_seqlens` and crashes the engine, on main too (reported and reproduced by subhashpolisetti). #60112 runs such batches eagerly; it needs a small rebase after this PR. - **GLM-4.1V-family image replays with video enabled (fixed by #65453):** capture pads `cu_seqlens` to `max_frames_per_batch` but image replays pad to `max_batch_size`, so GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash image outputs are wrong when video is enabled, on main too. The image correctness checks above ran with video disabled. - vorapolsiloai's MI355X serving numbers posted below were for an earlier revision (startup timing probe). **Not a duplicate.** #65084 (merged) shares capture buffers but keeps greedy multi-replay dispatch; this PR builds on it. #65351 is a similar buffer-sharing change. #66067 (stacked on this PR) moves the per-model encoder CUDA graph code into shared mixins. ---

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bound MooncakeStoreConnector prefix lookups with a configurable deadline and a circuit breaker, so a slow or unavailable store returns cache misses instead of holding up the scheduler indefinitely.

## Claims

- `kv_connector_extra_config.lookup_timeout_s` bounds blocking, async and prefetched lookups, including executor queue time; the default is 1 second.
- Three consecutive RPC failures open the breaker for 30 seconds. After cooldown, one probe is admitted; queue expiry does not count as a store failure.
- Late replies are ignored, cached outcomes update the breaker once, and the reset RPC has a 60-second deadline.

## Validation

- 30 CPU regressions passed with `python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_lookup.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -k 'lookup or prefetch or circuit_breaker or cached_hit' -q` in a uv-managed Python 3.12 environment. These include real local ZMQ sockets and the existing lookup/prefetch integration tests.
- Repository hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, markdownlint and test tethering.
- Real Mooncake-master and GPU validation remains pending. This stays a draft; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Incorporates Nicolò Lucchesi's adjustments from https://github.com/hj-mistral/vllm/pull/5. Configuration now uses one connector key rather than three environment variables; breaker threshold/cooldown remain constants. The breaker lives in the existing KV connector utilities, and the CPU-marked tests run in the existing V1 Others step without an extra CI job.

Queue expiry returns a cache miss without penalizing a healthy but busy master. A half-open probe prevents a recovery burst, and an abandoned probe releases its slot after one timeout window. Only new lookups are gated, allowing pending requests to read their results.

The reset request reuses the bounded socket helper and allows longer for the server to drain saves. Its existing caller contract still requires in-flight work to be drained before reset. This change bounds client waits; it does not cancel an RPC already executing on the master or change KV load/save behavior.

Two existing integration tests were aligned with the multipart reset helper and the new default: the TTL test explicitly keeps its RPC deadline beyond its simulated TTL expiry.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Refresh streaming request keys after preemption
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With lookahead block hashing, a streaming input continuation can replace a token included in a cached block's hash. If the request is preempted, the scheduler recomputes its block hashes from the current tokens, but `OffloadingConnector` retains its previously recorded keys. It can then look up stale entries or skip storing the recomputed KV, causing later requests to miss the CPU cache and recompute the prefix.

Before looking up a resumed request, clear each group's offload keys and rebuild them from the current block hashes.

This is a follow-up to lookahead hash support in #61589 and #64096.

## Claims

- Offload lookups use the recomputed hashes after a streaming request resumes.
- All group keys are rebuilt from the current block hashes.

## Validation

On `main` at `0db3734d51`, the new unit test fails before the fix because the connector retains the old key, and passes with the fix.

<details>
<summary>Unit test</summary>

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

</details>

**End-to-end:** Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP with one speculative token, `OffloadingConnector`, and NVIDIA GB10. A two-part streaming request was resumed with `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True, reset_connector=False)`. After it completed, the GPU prefix cache was reset and a second request reused the resulting prefix.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Second request's CPU cache hit | 0 tokens | 576 tokens |
| Second request's output tokens | `[198, 196, 196]` | `[198, 196, 196]` |

Before the fix, three KV groups had the new key but the MTP group did not, so the prefix could not be loaded. With the fix, all four groups hit and the 576-token prefix was loaded from CPU. This is a single functional run, not a latency benchmark.

## Details

While a streaming request's KV remains resident, its existing hash still describes that KV. When the request restarts from zero computed tokens, the core scheduler recomputes hashes for the current token sequence. The connector previously only appended keys, leaving already-recorded positions unchanged.

For resumable requests with lookahead hashing, the connector clears each group's recorded keys and uses the existing update logic to rebuild them from the current hashes.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail never-sent fetches locally
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Queued P2P Fetch messages can outlive a cancelled or timed-out load and be flushed after a delayed handshake. Retire never-sent loads locally and release the producer's parked storage without closing newer work using the same request ID.

Extracts **A** from #61667 as requested in review. Refs #61532. B (#64299) and C (#64300) have merged; this PR addresses the separate unsent-fetch lifecycle.

## Claims

- Retired, cancelled or expired Fetch messages never reach transport handoff.
- Never-sent loads fail locally without abort/deferred-release work. Producer terminal release cannot close a newer live round.
- Post-disconnect AbortAck semantics and finished-request failure bookkeeping are preserved.

## Validation

Tested on main `9cd2e98b595e` with cu130 artifacts from `b2a9480dc7aa` (identical native sources), Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| P2P and tiering component suites after test trimming | 467 passed |
| Repository hooks, including mypy, docs lint and CI tethering | Passed |
| Previously recorded real-weight LLM regression, commit `e388466c` | Passed |
| Previously recorded real-weight baseline control | Failed: peer received the retired fetch |

Reproduce the retained suite from a configured checkout:

```bash
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 UCX_TLS=tcp,self .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
```

The retained manager regression verifies that a never-sent fetch fails locally and releases parked producer blocks. Session regressions cover cancellation/expiry, both handshake orderings, finished-request propagation, subsequent ID reuse, expiry logging and dead-connection/send-failure handling.

Earlier real-entry validation used real HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M weights at `93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2`, RTX 4060 Ti/CUDA 13.0, FP16/eager/greedy/batch-invariant inference and NIXL UCX TCP localhost. A delayed-handshake request timed out and recomputed; the peer then received a fresh fetch and never the retired one. The equivalent control observed `['retired', 'live']` and failed. That model test and its dedicated fixture were removed from CI per [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64298#issuecomment-6630803920), because the smaller manager/session suite covers the same flow. Their source remains in `e388466c`; the production code is unchanged by this test-only trimming. No task-accuracy or performance claim is made.

## Details

Track a queued Fetch by object identity until transport handoff. Timeout or cancellation retires it locally. Empty terminal Fetch messages release producer supply, subject to the existing-request guard so they cannot close newer work. The manager handles terminal-only fetches without replaying stale stores. Finished loads keep #64300's `request_finished` marker, and the liveness check applies only to data Fetch messages so #64251's abort acknowledgements remain sendable after disconnect.

Duplicate-work check: this is the requested split from the original PR. Merged #64256 handles timed-out sent loads and deferred slot release; merged B handles buffered terminals, and merged C handles finished-request failures. This PR covers the separate never-sent path.

Rendered behavior documentation is in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`. The existing `v1-kv-offload` CI step selects the retained tests and covers the changed sources.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen2.5-Omni] Size the video encoder budget from the processor's video limits
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen2.5-Omni has the same video budget gap that #66017 fixed for Qwen3-Omni. It sizes the video encoder budget and the profiling dummy from the image limits (3584x3584 frames), while its HF processor caps video frames at `768 * 28 * 28` pixels (`Qwen2_5OmniProcessorKwargs`). So the budget stops short of `max_model_len` when `max_model_len` isn't a multiple of the two-frame step, and startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a ~1.5k-token dummy video. This moves the video sizing from #66017 into Qwen2.5-Omni and lets Qwen3-Omni inherit it.

## Claims

The two failures have different causes:

- At `--max-model-len 24000` the admission limit is wrong. A synthetic 30 s 896x504 video at 2 fps (17,280 video tokens) is rejected with `exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384`; with this PR the budget reaches 24,000 and it is served.
- At the default 32768 the admission limit is already right, but startup profiling runs the vision encoder on a 1,458-token dummy. On an NVIDIA A10 (23 GB), a synthetic 56 s 896x504 video (32,256 video tokens, admitted) then runs the vision encoder out of memory. With this PR the dummy fills the budget (within one two-frame step), profiling reserves that memory, and the video is served.
- Trade-off: the reserved encoder memory comes out of the KV cache, -19% at 24k and -28% at 32k on the A10 (below). The default context still starts there. Deployments with shorter videos can lower the reservation with the `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hints in the [memory docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/conserving_memory/#configurable-options); at 32k, `{"count": 1, "num_frames": 32, "width": 640, "height": 360}` brings the profiled video from 32,256 to 4,784 tokens.
- With a `limit_mm_per_prompt` video size hint, for the configurations checked, the dummy produces the same number of video tokens as a real video of that size. Checked on CPU for Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni with 11 hint sizes (portrait, landscape, narrow, oversized, tiny) under no processor kwargs, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`, scoped `images_kwargs.size` and both scoped settings, plus `do_resize=False` (flat, scoped to videos, scoped to images) for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni: 205 of 205 cases match, against 150 mismatches on main. Some Clef-Omni inputs fail with `do_resize=False`, on main as well, because frame capping can produce dimensions incompatible with patchification. This also fixes Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni on main, where a 540x960 hint on Qwen3-Omni was profiled at 408 tokens per frame pair vs 510 for a real video.
- Images are unchanged (budget 16,384). Without size hints, Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni profiling is unchanged.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni.py` use the real Qwen2.5-Omni-3B processor: the budget reaches `max_model_len` at 20000 and 24000, a 30 s video fits at 24000, the profiling dummy fills the budget at 4096 / 16384 / 24000, the video canvas matches what processing produces (no override, flat `max_pixels`, scoped `videos_kwargs.size`), a size-hinted dummy matches a real video of that size, and the image budget is unchanged. `test_qwen3_omni.py` gets the size-hint test for Qwen3-Omni and Clef-Omni. With main's model files, 17 of the 22 new tests fail; the image test and four size-hint cases that main already handles pass on both.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py   # 38 passed (22 new)
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni_mrope.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_audio_in_video.py   # 58 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "Qwen2.5-Omni or Qwen3-Omni or clef"   # 17 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # passes
```

End to end on an NVIDIA A10 (23 GB) with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B`, synthetic random-pixel videos, `limit_mm_per_prompt` image 0 / video 1 / audio 0, default `max_num_batched_tokens` (8192) and `gpu_memory_utilization`, the same wheel with only `qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py` swapped. This ran on the first commit; the second commit only changes profiling when a size hint is set, and the dummy without hints is identical (same `video_grid_thw` at 4096 / 16384 / 24000 / 32768 for all three models).

| `max_model_len` | request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24000 | 30 s 896x504 video (17,280 video tokens) | `VLLMValidationError: ... 17280 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384` | served (17,294 prompt tokens) |
| 32768 | 10 s 896x504 video | served | served, same greedy text |
| 32768 | 56 s 896x504 video (32,256 video tokens) | `CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 630.00 MiB` in the vision encoder (`_process_video_input`) | served (32,270 prompt tokens) |

| `max_model_len` | encoder budget main → PR | KV cache memory main → PR | KV cache tokens main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24000 | 16,384 → 24,000 | 13.45 → 10.83 GiB | 335,872 → 221,183 |
| 32768 | 32,768 → 32,768 | 13.44 → 9.71 GiB | 335,872 → 163,840 |

## Details

- Root cause: `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo` inherits the Qwen2-VL video estimate, which sizes frames at the largest image and adds two-frame steps of 16,384 tokens until `seq_len`, so at 24000 it stops at 16,384. Processing then shrinks real frames to the processor's video default, which is also why the dummy video only reaches 729 tokens per step.
- Default sizing: the video methods #66017 added to `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerProcessingInfo` move to `Qwen2_5OmniThinkerProcessingInfo`, keyed by `processor_kwargs_cls`, and Qwen3-Omni inherits them; its dummy builder goes back to the alias it was before #66017.
- Size hints: a hinted frame is resolved with the video processor's settings (`get_video_frame_size`: `smart_resize` within the video limits, the hinted size when the video `do_resize` is off, and Clef-Omni's own frame cap) instead of being clamped per dimension against the landscape video canvas. With resizing enabled, Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni resolve hinted dimensions within the video processor's pixel limits, so an oversized hint doesn't allocate a full-size dummy; with `do_resize=False` the hinted dimensions are kept, as processing keeps them.
- #63374 (Qwen2.5-Omni ViT CUDA graphs) reads `get_num_frames_with_most_features` through the Qwen2.5-VL encoder graph code. With this change it returns 84 frames at 32k with one video per prompt (4 on main), and 2 with the default video limit (1 on main).
- The shared Qwen2-VL estimate has the same budget gap for Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL at `max_model_len` values that aren't a multiple of the step. I kept this PR to the Omni models and can follow up on that one.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix dots_ocr vision tower QKV split for TP > 1
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `DotsVisionAttention` used a QKV-split helper meant for a differently sharded layer, scrambling q/k/v at TP > 1 so `dots.ocr` repeated one sentence for every image region. Split the local shard instead. Fixes #64541. ## Claims - `DotsVisionAttention` now splits QKV correctly under TP: TP=2 with the default weight-sharded encoder matches the TP=1 reference again. Confirmed on Ascend 910B3 (12/12 layout blocks) and on CUDA (2× A800, byte-identical output). - No behaviour change at TP=1: the previous helper degenerated to the same local `chunk(3)`, which is why single-card serving was already correct. - Adds a `dots_ocr` entry to the VLM generation tests with `tensor_parallel_size=2`, marked `pytest.mark.skip` because the HF reference side cannot run under the pinned transformers version (see below). - Also covers `dots.mocr`: it ships a byte-identical `config.json` (`architectures: ["DotsOCRForCausalLM"]`, `model_type: dots_ocr`, same vision tower dims) and is served by this same file, so it carries the same TP>1 defect. ## Validation ### End-to-end reproducer (before/after, 2× Ascend 910B3, vLLM 0.30.0) Same image, prompt and sampling parameters in all runs: | # | code | TP | mm encoder | result | |---|------|----|-----------|--------| | 0 | before | 2 | weights (default) | broken: 4× identical "I am sorry ... blurry image of a person" | | 1 | before | 2 | `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` | correct: 12 layout blocks | | 2 | after | 2 | weights (default) | correct: 12 layout blocks | | 3 | before | 1 | weights | correct: 12 layout blocks (reference) | Run 1 bypasses the vision *weight* TP path (`disable_tp=True`, the encoder sees `tp_size == 1`), which isolates the failure to the TP-sharded ViT rather than to the LM or the processor. After the fix, run 2 matches run 3: - 12/12 layout blocks with identical categories and bounding boxes; - extracted text identical character-for-character except for one empty `` cell in a different column inside a table row (same length, sampling at `temperature=0.1`); - 52 s for the full page versus 8 s for the degenerate pre-fix output. A CPU-only script in the issue shows the same layout mismatch without any accelerator (it only simulates the all-gather + `chunk(3)` on a token-index tensor). ### Fix confirmed on CUDA (2× A800 80GB PCIe) Environment: vLLM 0.32.0, torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.105.08, 2× A800 80GB PCIe (sm_80, PCIe interconnect), model `rednote-hilab/dots.ocr` (6.08 GB, 2 shards), OpenAI-compatible server with `--max-model-len 4096 --trust-remote-code`, sampling `temperature=0.1`, `seed=0`. The image was a synthetic A4 layout page (title, two-column body, 3×3 table), not the document used in the NPU run, so the post-fix result is compared against the TP=1 reference for the same image instead of block counts. | # | code | TP | mm encoder | output len | repeated-paragraph rate | matches TP=1 ref | latency | |---|------|----|-----------|-----------|------------------------|------------------|---------| | 0 | before | 2 | weights | 6095 | 93% | no | 6.6 s | | 1 | after | 2 | weights | 1117 | 0% | yes, byte-identical | 1.7 s | | 2 | before | 2 | `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` | 1117 | 0% | yes | 1.6 s | | 3 | before | 1 | weights | 1117 | 0% | reference | 3.6 s | | 4 | after | 1 | weights | 1117 | 0% | yes | 2.0 s | - Pre-fix TP=2 with the default weight-sharded encoder reproduces the reported failure: the same paragraph is emitted 6+ times regardless of image content. - Post-fix TP=2 output is byte-for-byte identical to the TP=1 reference. - The `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` control was unaffected before the fix, which isolates the defect to the TP-sharded vision weights rather than the LM or the processor. - TP=1 output is unchanged by the patch. The degenerate text differs from the NPU run ("license plate" paragraph vs. "I am sorry ... blurry image of a person"). Both are attractor states reached when the vision embeddings are noise, and the failure mode — identical text for every image region — is the same. Note: this run applied the two-state patch (PR diff on/off) to the installed 0.32.0 wheel instead of building this branch from source, because the container had no `nvcc`. `dots_ocr.py` in the 0.30/0.31/0.32 releases still contains the same pre-fix `split_qkv` call, so the two states are semantically the PR's before/after. ### Regression test A `dots_ocr` entry is added to `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py` with `tensor_parallel_size=2`, behind: ```python pytest.mark.skip(reason="Custom model code is not compatible with Transformers v5") ``` That is the same class of breakage as the existing skips in this file (`ultravox`, `kimi_vl`, …). dots.ocr's remote code declares `transformers_version: 4.51.0`, while vLLM now requires `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.23.0`, and it breaks in two layers on the reference side: `generate()` rejects `mm_token_type_ids` as an unused kwarg, and once that is stripped, `prepare_inputs_for_generation` does not handle a `None` `cache_position`. The entry is kept rather than dropped so the intended TP>1 coverage is recorded and can be enabled once the remote code supports transformers v5. Separately, the vision tower also trips the CI GPU-sync checker at three host copies. That is an independent property of the model — it runs under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which the CI image sets globally — not something this diff introduces, and it is tracked in #66243 together with the plan for a dedicated, HF-free regression test. ## Details ### Root cause `DotsVisionAttention` builds its QKV with `QKVParallelLinear`, so each TP rank already owns the local `[q | k | v]` shard. It nevertheless called `Qwen2VisionAttention.split_qkv()`, a helper written for Qwen2-VL's `ColumnParallelLinear`, where each rank holds a *slice of the whole packed* `[q | k | v]` tensor. At TP > 1 that helper all-gathers and re-splits: ``` QKVParallelLinear (TP=2): [q0 k0 v0] | [q1 k1 v1] all_gather(dim=-1): [q0 k0 v0 | q1 k1 v1] chunk(3): (q0+k0), (v0+q1), (k1+v1) rank0 -> q=q0 (ok), k=v0 (wrong), v=k1 (wrong) rank1 -> q=k0 (wrong), k=q1 (wrong), v=v1 (ok) ``` The vision embeddings become noise, so the LM collapses to a fixed sentence for every region. At TP=1 the helper degenerates to a plain `chunk(3)` on the full tensor, which is why single-card serving was correct. ### Fix `DotsVisionAttention.forward` splits the local tensor directly (`x.chunk(3, dim=-1)` + reshape), exactly as `glm_ocr.py` already does for the same attention layout. ### Scope and risk - Diff is 32 added / 2 deleted lines across two files; no core component is touched. - TP=1 output is unchanged by construction. - `dots.mocr` (`dots-studio/dots.mocr`) ships a byte-identical `config.json` and the same `architectures` entry, so vLLM dispatches it to this same model class and it gets the same fix. The Ascend reproducer used `dots.mocr`; the A800 run used `dots.ocr` itself. - Only the default (weight-sharded) encoder path was broken; users on `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` were unaffected. - Verified on two independent backends (Ascend 910B3 and CUDA A800); the CUDA run also confirms TP=1 output is unchanged. ### Related work No duplicate: #63074 (`dots.ocr: support encoder CUDA graph`) is open and edits other hunks of `dots_ocr.py` (CUDA-graph wiring), not the QKV split, so the two PRs are trivially rebasable on each other. ---

The automated test is added but skipped: dots.ocr's remote code targets transformers 4.51 and cannot run under the pinned transformers 5.x, which is why the rest of this file uses the same skip reason. ## Overview

Aligns the Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe's MI355X section with [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4887](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4887), the per-concurrency retune of the K3.1 MI355X vLLM AgentX lane on the recipe's own `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k31` image (`sha256:5f47cc10…`).

## Claims

- **New preset `mi355x_agentx_c1` ("AgentX TP8, concurrency 1").** It follows #4887's concurrency-1 point:
  - Plain TP8 with no DCP; #4887 moves this point from DCP8 to DCP1.
  - KV cache on the GPU; KV offload is off.
  - The K3.1 DSpark draft with 7 tokens and block rejection.
  - `decode_backend: latency_specialized` together with `kda_prefill_backend: fused`.
  - `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`.
  - Decode-only capture sizes 2–16, with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`.
  - BF16 linear layers, MoE combine and all-reduce.
  - #4887's full env (including the DCP and offload variables the point inherits from the lane's base env), `--seed 7`, `--moe-backend auto` and `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`, so the rendered command is the one InferenceX ran.
- **`mi355x_agentx` (concurrency 48) now follows #4887's concurrency-48 point** instead of the best-performance band:
  - BF16 precision as the K3.1 policy requires: `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` INT4 → `NONE` (and `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB` dropped), `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8` 1 → 0, the FP8 KDA `in_proj` `--quantization-config` dropped, and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32` added.
  - The DSpark draft goes from 5 to 3 tokens with block rejection, and the decode capture sizes from 6–288 (step 6) to 4–192 (step 4).
  - `--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.92 → 0.91; `mla_prefill_backend` is no longer named (ROCm picks `ROCM_AITER_FA` first anyway).
  - Adds #4887's `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`, `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1`, `THP_MEM_ALLOC_ENABLE=1`, `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200`, `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1`, `--seed 7`, `--moe-backend auto` and `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`.
  - Its synthetic-acceptance snippet uses the golden acceptance length for 3 draft tokens, 2.88.
- **Bug fix, already on main.** Turning on Low-latency decode with `mi355x_agentx` replaced the preset's `--additional-config` (the builder keeps the last occurrence of a flag), so `kda_prefill_backend: fused` was silently dropped. Both MI355X presets now merge it through `json_args`. `mi355x_agentx` also turns the feature off explicitly, because its config doesn't meet the MI355X path's limits.
- **Low-latency decode docs.** They now describe the MI355X (FlyDSL) path and its startup limits, taken from `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode`:
  - Speculative decoding is required.
  - `--max-num-seqs` must be 1, 2, 4 or 8, with `--max-num-seqs` × (1 + draft tokens) ≤ 16.
  - The KDA recurrent state must be FP32, and no KV offload connector is allowed.
  - Without DCP, only 3 or 7 draft tokens at `--max-num-seqs` 1 or 2.
- **Synthetic acceptance.** The snippets now use InferenceX's K3.1 DSpark golden acceptance lengths (`infx/golden_al_distribution/kimi-k3.1-pro__dspark__kimi-k3.1-pro-dspark-preview__probabilistic-block.yaml`): 2.88 for 3 draft tokens and 3.69 for 7, instead of 3.62, which is Kimi-K3's value.
- **Wording.** The stale MI355X guide text ("so far only AgentX TP8 has run") is updated, and both MI355X preset labels now name their concurrency.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm` from vllm-project/recipes main reports the recipes valid.
- The vllm-project/recipes site tests pass on this content: presets, schema, dcp-selector, kv-offload, hardware, guide-html, overlay, context, pd-connectors, smg-pd and ppu-platform.
- The rendered commands match #4887's effective configs (base merged with the override, at head `336f121`), checked flag by flag and env var by env var: `mi355x_agentx_c1` against `override_gpu_kv_c1` (24 args, 25 env vars) and `mi355x_agentx` against `override_dram_c48` (28 args, 25 env vars, including the `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` config). The only difference is `--served-model-name`, which equals the model ID.
- #4887 CI sweep ([run 42371416815](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/42371416815)) at concurrency 1 against the earlier TP8×DCP8 config: 1,839.1 vs 1,792.2 tok/s/GPU (+2.6 %), and 1/P90 TPOT 201.6 vs 194.6 (+3.6 %).

## Details

- **#4887 is still open.** The runbook says the preset follows #4887 and has only been measured on the image digest it names. If #4887 changes before it merges, this preset should follow.
- **Public vLLM main can't run this preset yet.** Main refuses latency_specialized without DCP for K3.1: it needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1` (`runtime/__init__.py`), and it refuses MLA layers that have an indexer (`runtime/guards.py`). So the preset runs only on the `kimi-k31` image; the runbook says this.
- **Left out on purpose:** #4887's concurrency 4–32 changes:
  - Concurrency 4: 7 draft tokens with `--max-num-seqs 2`.
  - Concurrency 10–32: `--max-num-seqs` set below the client concurrency.

  These shape the server to the AgentX client rather than describing a serving setup. Concurrency 10 also regresses about 8 % in #4887's own sweep.
- **Possible conflict:** #65958 (MI325X) edits the same `low_latency_decode.hardware` block, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Reserve kpool decode indexer logits in workspace during profiling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #64874.

Serving `GLM-5.3-Flash` on ROCm crashes in decode once `batch_size * next_n * max_pool_len * 4` outgrows both the prefill K-gather workspace and the largest captured CUDA graph batch (`AssertionError: Workspace is locked but allocation from 'rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:...:rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits' requires 276.00 MB, current size is 265.00 MB`).

## Claims

- reserve the worst-case decode logits buffer on `current_workspace_manager()` during `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool`'s profiling pass, matching `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`, and keep the `torch.empty` reservation for the `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` prefill logits cap.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v -s tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py -k decode_logits_workspace

# serve + benchmark (96 concurrent decode requests -> 576 decode rows -> 288.00 MB)
# with or without --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' is the same, the bug doesn't depends on mm inputs
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --port 8025

vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8025 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2200 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-prefix-len 2150 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 96 --ignore-eos
```

| workload | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unit test (`16 seqs x 6 = 96` decode rows, `max_pool_len=4096`) | `AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... requires 1.50 MB, current size is 1.27 MB` | passed |
| `GLM-5.3-Flash` e2e (`max_model_len=524288`, `max_num_seqs=128`, `MTP=5`, 92 concurrent requests = 552 decode rows) | `AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... requires 276.00 MB, current size is 265.00 MB` | 92/92 requests completed (locked workspace 384.00 MB) |

## Details

On ROCm, `sparse_attn_indexer_kpool` calls `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(..., max_model_len=max_pool_len)` on decode, which takes `out_logits` of shape `(batch_size * next_n, max_pool_len)` in `float32` (or `(heads, batch_size * next_n, max_pool_len)` on the stage-1 fallback) from `current_workspace_manager()`. Its profiling branch (`if not isinstance(attn_metadata, dict):`) was copied from the CUDA implementation, where DeepGEMM allocates decode logits through the PyTorch caching allocator (`torch.empty`), so the ROCm workspace only ever saw the prefill K-gather buffers before `lock_workspace()`.

commits.pr_title: [Core][KVConnector] Keep the offloaded KV tier across pause/sleep
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`pause`/`sleep` exist to hand GPU memory back. An external KV connector tier
(CPU/SSD offload) is the one cache that *survives* that handover, and the
pause/sleep cascade evicts it. For an RL rollout that time-shares the GPU
(`sleep(1)` → train → `wake_up()`), that tier is what makes resumption cheap:
without it the resume re-prefills every in-flight sample.

Whether the tier is still valid depends on the caller replacing the weights,
which the engine cannot know at pause time. Block hashes do not cover the
weights, so the default stays "evict" and this adds an opt-out:

```python
llm.sleep(level=1, clear_connector_cache=False)   # same weights on wake-up
```

Threaded through `pause_scheduler`/`sleep` to `_reset_caches(reset_connector=)`,
the Python and Rust clients, and `/pause` and `/sleep`. Default `True`
everywhere, so nothing changes unless a caller opts out. The Rust client sends
the argument only when opting out, so a new frontend still drives an older
engine.

## Measured

2x GB200, slurm job 30001, on the nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`
(`0.29.1rc1.dev422`), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this branch's files bind-mounted
over the image one by one (mounting the whole package would hide the compiled
`_C` that ships in it).

Server, on the head node's 4 GPUs:

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve $MODEL --served-model-name dsv41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --port 8712 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":128,"cpu_bytes_to_use":34359738368}}'
```

Client, from the second node: 16 concurrent completions of ~19.5k tokens each
(311,744 tokens queried in total), then `/sleep?level=1` with and without
`&clear_connector_cache=false`, then `/wake_up`, then the same 16 prompts
again. Full script in the details block below.

| replay after wake-up | default | `clear_connector_cache=false` |
|---|---|---|
| external prefix-cache hits | **0** / 311,744 | **311,296** / 311,744 |
| `kv_offload_load_bytes_total` | 0 | **1.31 GB** |
| `kv_offload_store_bytes_total` | 1.31 GB (all recomputed) | 0 |
| p50 latency | 4.421 s | 0.490 s |

The counters are the evidence: with the tier cleared the replay stores the same
1.31 GB all over again, with it kept it reads exactly that 1.31 GB back. The
latency column is indicative only — the two arms run in sequence against one
server and share prompts, so the second arm starts warmer.

Two things about this run that a reviewer should know:

- The patch set mounted into the image also carried #57813, so the connector
  config above additionally had `"pin_in_flight_chunks": true`, which is that
  PR's key and not part of this one. It cannot have moved these numbers: the
  run stores 1.22 GiB into a 32 GiB tier, so nothing is ever evicted and
  pinning has nothing to do. Reproducing this PR alone means dropping that key,
  as the command above does.
- The client's prompt generator counts words, not tokens, so `--prompt-tokens
  4096` produces ~19.5k tokens per request. The absolute latencies depend on
  that; the hit/miss counters do not.

<details>
<summary>Client script</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Does the offloaded KV tier survive a sleep, and does a resume reuse it?

Sequence per arm:
  1. warm N distinct long prefixes (they land in the CPU tier),
  2. sleep(level=1) -- with or without clear_connector_cache,
  3. wake_up,
  4. replay the same prefixes and read the external-cache hit counters.

With the tier kept, step 4 hits the offloaded blocks; with it cleared, step 4
re-prefills from scratch. The difference is the point of PR #57810.
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import requests


def metrics(base: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    out: dict[str, float] = {}
    for line in requests.get(f"{base}/metrics", timeout=30).text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("#") or " " not in line:
            continue
        name, _, value = line.rpartition(" ")
        if "prefix_cache" in name or "offload" in name or "connector" in name:
            try:
                out[name] = out.get(name, 0.0) + float(value)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return out


def prompt(idx: int, tokens: int) -> str:
    # Distinct prefixes, long enough to fill several offload chunks.
    return f"session-{idx}: " + " ".join(f"w{idx}_{i}" for i in range(tokens))


def fire(base: str, idx: int, tokens: int, max_tokens: int = 8) -> float:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(
        f"{base}/v1/completions",
        json={
            "model": "dsv41",
            "prompt": prompt(idx, tokens),
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": 0.0,
        },
        timeout=600,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return time.perf_counter() - t0


def run_arm(base: str, keep_tier: bool, n: int, tokens: int) -> dict:
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as pool:
        warm = list(pool.map(lambda i: fire(base, i, tokens), range(n)))
    before = metrics(base)

    params = {"level": 1, "mode": "abort"}
    if keep_tier:
        params["clear_connector_cache"] = "false"
    requests.post(f"{base}/sleep", params=params, timeout=600).raise_for_status()
    requests.post(f"{base}/wake_up", timeout=600).raise_for_status()

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as pool:
        replay = list(pool.map(lambda i: fire(base, i, tokens), range(n)))
    after = metrics(base)

    delta = {k: after.get(k, 0.0) - before.get(k, 0.0) for k in set(before) | set(after)}
    return {
        "keep_tier": keep_tier,
        "warm_p50_s": sorted(warm)[len(warm) // 2],
        "replay_p50_s": sorted(replay)[len(replay) // 2],
        "metric_delta": {k: v for k, v in sorted(delta.items()) if v},
    }


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--prompt-tokens", type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    base = f"http://{args.host}:{args.port}"
    result = {
        "cleared": run_arm(base, False, args.requests, args.prompt_tokens),
        "kept": run_arm(base, True, args.requests, args.prompt_tokens),
    }
    result["verdict"] = (
        "tier reused on resume"
        if result["kept"]["replay_p50_s"] < result["cleared"]["replay_p50_s"]
        else "no measurable difference"
    )
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        json.dump(result, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

`_reset_caches` / the connector eviction on pause is untouched by any open PR.
#57296 is KV *event* payloads, #56754 is request draining, #49789 is
graph/runtime state across weight reloads.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q                          # 177 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q          # 467 passed
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -q -k "pause or sleep_forwards"  # 10 passed
cargo test -p vllm-server -- pause_route sleep_route                # 5 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed>                                   # passed
```

The rest of `test_engine_core.py` starts a real engine and does not run on my
box (another process holds the GPU: "Free memory on device cuda:0 (92.93/139.8
GiB) ... less than desired GPU memory utilization"). CI covers it.

`test_pause_clear_connector_cache_opt_out` covers both values through
`EngineCore.pause_scheduler`; `test_pause_forwards_connector_flag` covers the
immediate and deferred `EngineCoreProc` paths and that an omitted argument
clears; `sleep_route_sends_connector_opt_out_only_when_requested` pins the Rust
wire format.

No model-quality impact: sampling, weights and attention are untouched.

## Review rounds

Adversarial automated review, several rounds.

**Round 1** rejected the original design (removing the eviction outright):
block hashes exclude the weight version and weight updates do not reset
connectors, so that eviction is what prevents stale KV — hence the opt-out. It
then found a P1 in the Rust client, which sent three positional arguments
unconditionally and broke `/pause` and `/sleep` against an older engine.

**A later round found a P1 that this revision fixes, and it is the reason the
connector file is in this diff.** Keeping the tier crashed the very case the
feature exists for:

```
sleep(level=1, mode="keep", clear_connector_cache=False) -> wake_up()
AssertionError at offloading/scheduler.py:1792
```

`_reset_caches` preempts the running requests, and `preempted_req_ids` is only
consumed by the *next* `schedule()`. Nothing is scheduled while the engine
sleeps, so that set survives the sleep and lands on the step that resumes the
request — and with the tier kept, that step already carries the request's
resume **load**. The preemption flush asserted that a preempted request can
only hold stores, which is true when preemption and resumption are separate
steps, and false here.

The flush now takes the store jobs and leaves the load alone: a load reads no
freed block, so it is not what the flush is there to settle. Default clearing
never reached this, because with the tier gone there is no load to find —
which is also why the completed-request measurement above could not have
caught it. `test_preempted_request_resumed_in_the_same_step` covers both
scheduling modes and fails on the previous revision.

### The opt-out is now refused where it is not safe

The flag reaches whatever connector is configured, and the same-step resume is
a state every connector that tracks per-request transfers has to expect. Only
`OffloadingConnector` does, after the fix above. `MooncakeStoreConnector` also
implements `reset_cache`, also consumes `preempted_req_ids`, and pops
`load_specs[req_id]` and `_unfinished_requests[req_id]` for them
(`mooncake/store/scheduler.py:226-231`) — the entries its new-request loop
then asserts on four lines later.

Rather than change a second connector I cannot exercise here, the opt-out is
fail-closed: connectors declare `supports_retained_cache_on_pause` (default
`False`, `True` on `OffloadingConnector`, the conjunction of its children on
`MultiConnector`), and a pause that asks to keep a cache the connector cannot
keep is refused before anything is paused:

```
MooncakeStoreConnector cannot keep its cache across a pause: the resume lands
in the step that reports the pause's preemptions, which this connector does
not expect. Drop clear_connector_cache=False.
```

Making Mooncake handle it is a separate, testable change; until then its users
get an error at the call instead of a crash at the wake-up.

Two related notes:

- This is the same interaction as #52360 (preemption vs in-flight transfers).
  This PR does not change the flush for stores, which is what protects against
  it. It does extend how long a bad entry would survive if a connector ever
  produced one, which is an argument for the default being "evict".
- Follow-up worth filing separately: nothing on the weight-update path
  force-evicts the tier. `finish_weight_update` doing so would remove the
  footgun at no false-positive cost.

The same round also asked for, and this revision adds, the `/pause` opt-out
wire test, a `sleep(level>=1)` threading test, the one-line note on why the
Python client may always send the argument (client and engine ship together,
so they cannot disagree), and the parameter's documentation on
`EngineCoreProc.pause_scheduler`, which is the docstring MP clients read.

A further round, told about all of the above, checked for any path where the
