commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Refactor encoder cuda graph to support share graph buffer reuse
commits.pr_body:
<!-- vLLM PR description format: Purpose / Test Plan / Test Result -->

## Purpose

Encoder CUDA graphs are captured once per token budget, and every captured graph allocates its own full set of I/O buffers sized by that budget. That per-budget O(budget) memory cost is the only reason the default budget table is a coarse power-of-2 ladder — which forces ~33% average padding waste (round-up to the next power of two).

This PR removes the memory cost **generically, with zero model changes**, following the decoder's `input_ids[:num_tokens]` pattern:

1. **Universal shared capture buffers.** At capture time the manager keeps the first (largest) budget's buffers per (path, axis) as the shared allocation; for every later budget it probes shapes via the model's unmodified `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs()` and, per buffer key, checks prefix compatibility (same ndim/trailing dims/dtype, rows fit). Compatible keys capture into a prefix view of the shared buffer (probe content is copied in so the capture-time forward sees correct metadata); incompatible keys silently keep their per-budget allocation. Scalars are shared by identity. This works because all encoder buffers are packed-contiguous row buffers and replay only ever writes `buf[:real_rows]`. Output buffers are shared the same way. No protocol changes, no model changes, no config knobs.

2. **Subdivided default budget table.** With extra graphs costing ~zero buffer memory, the auto-inferred default becomes a subdivided table (4 steps per octave up to 1024, 2 above; 64→16384 = 25 tiers, expected padding waste ~10% vs ~33% for power-of-2). Explicit `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` still overrides. Capture-time cost is one extra forward per extra tier; the existing 64-graph warning covers capture-axes blowups.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR covers encoder-graph buffer sharing; complements #41714 (pool memory in profiling) and follows the padding-semantics precedent of #42796.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit + capture/replay (GPU)
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q
# E2E incl. real-weights Qwen2.5-VL (image+video) and DSV4.1 dummy
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k "deepseek_v41 or qwen2_5_vl" -x -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

New coverage: `TestDefaultBudgetTable` (subdivided default, user override, `max_vision_items` path), `TestSharedCaptureBuffers` (one storage across budgets with a **completely unmodified** mock model, prefix views, shared output slicing, large→small→large replay equivalence vs eager, `clear()` releases), `TestSharedBufferFallback` (an incompatible-shaped buffer falls back to its own allocation while other keys still share; scalars shared by identity).

Performance measured on one idle 4×GB200 (SM100) Slurm node, TP=4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (dummy weights; timing is shape-exact), baseline/patched interleaved on the same node.

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: **80 passed** (GPU).
- e2e: **3 passed, 1 skipped** (DSV4.1 video skip is pre-existing upstream).

### Capture cost (DSV4.1, TP=4, per-rank)

| Run | Budget table | Encoder graphs | Capture memory | Capture time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upstream default | pow2, 9 tiers | 9 | 4.19 GiB | 14 s |
| **This PR (default)** | **25 tiers, subdivided** | **25** | **3.80 GiB** | 21 s |

The dense table's 16 extra graphs cost zero buffer memory, and total capture memory ends up *below* the upstream default (Σbudgets ≈ 2×max → 1×max for encoder buffers) at a one-time +7 s capture cost.

### Request latency (concurrency-1 probes, medians of interleaved rounds)

| Probe | pow2 | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| pad2_heavy: 5×1344² imgs, 5120 tok (8192 → 6144 tier) | 577.9 / 570.2 ms | 569.0 / 553.0 ms | ~-2-3% |
| mid_pad: 1×714² img (512 → 320 tier) | 134.6 / 136.6 ms | 138.7 / 135.9 ms | neutral |
| no_pad control (994 tok → 1024 both) | 211.4 / 214.8 ms | 223.0 / 215.7 ms | neutral |
| cliff_900 (508 tok → 512 tier both) | 159.6 / 157.3 ms | 162.0 / 156.5 ms | neutral |

VisionArena-Chat TTFT at concurrency 1: medians identical (~127-129 ms); means are dominated by warmup-order noise (an established property of this benchmark on this cluster).

### Notes / caveats

- The latency win scales with per-batch padding; high-padding workloads (multi-image requests landing just above a power of two) gain a few percent, everything else is neutral. The structural point of this PR is making fine-grained budgets free (memory), not the probe numbers.
- Prefix-incompatible buffers (hypothetical; none among the 21 current encoder-CG models) degrade gracefully to per-budget allocation.
- `docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md` is updated accordingly.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Keep FA sliding window active under batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, keep FlashAttention's sliding window active in every step, so Gemma-2 outputs on H100 (FA3) no longer depend on which requests share the batch.

Fixes #65587

## Claims

- Fixes #65587: under batch invariance, a sliding-window request on FA3 gives the same tokens and bitwise-equal logprobs alone as when it decodes next to other requests' prefill chunks.
- A 9-line change in `FlashAttentionImpl.forward`. It only runs with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on layers that have a sliding window; every other configuration is unchanged.
- Adds `test_sliding_window_logprobs_bitwise_alone_vs_mixed_batch` to `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py`, which the existing H100 and B200 batch invariance CI jobs already run.

## Validation

[@imthomp ran the fix on an H100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65627#issuecomment-6634783966) (vLLM nightly 0.33.0rc1.dev454 plus this diff): the issue reproducer went from 5/20 differing prompts to 0/20. The first version of the new test passed there without the fix too. Its targets were 8–14 tokens, so each decode step read fewer than 64 KV tokens. That is a single KV tile for both FA3 kernels, and with one tile they produce identical bits. The second commit lengthens the targets to 233–393 tokens and the fillers to 1.2k–1.7k tokens. Every prompt stays below the 4096-token window: a sequence longer than the window makes the mixed steps it is part of keep the window too, which hides the bug in those steps. **H100 results for the updated test are still to be filled in.**

FA3 needs SM90 and only A100s were available to me. FA2 runs there and uses the same KV tile either way, so the bug does not reproduce on A100. To check the updated test's workload without an H100, I recorded the `max_seqlen_k` and window that the sliding-window layers actually pass to the FA kernel, and applied FA3's host-side kernel selection to them (trace below).

| Check (A100-SXM4-80GB unless noted) | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| Issue reproducer on H100 (`google/gemma-2-9b-it`), prompts that differ (@imthomp) | 5/20 | 0/20 |
| Existing batch invariance tests on `google/gemma-2-2b-it`, FLASH_ATTN, on H100 (@imthomp) | not run | 8 passed |
| First version of the new test on H100 (@imthomp) | passed | passed |
| Updated new test on H100 (FA3) | TODO, expected to fail | TODO, expected to pass |
| Updated new test on A100 (FA2) | passed | passed |
| Target decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched, from the trace of the updated test's workload | all 60 (15 per target) | 0 |
| Issue reproducer on A100 with H100 scheduler defaults, prompts that differ | 0/20 | 0/20 |
| Existing batch invariance tests on `google/gemma-2-2b-it`, FLASH_ATTN (`max_model_len` 2048 to 8192) | not run | 8 passed |
| `test_sliding_window_backend_correctness` (batch invariance off) | not run | 18 passed |

Commands (from `tests/`, with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`):

```bash
# New regression test
pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_sliding_window_logprobs_bitwise_alone_vs_mixed_batch

# Existing batch invariance tests on a sliding-window model
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=google/gemma-2-2b-it pytest -v -s v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -k "FLASH_ATTN and not test_sliding_window"

# Sliding-window attention backend correctness
pytest -q v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k test_sliding_window_backend_correctness

# Reproducer script from #65587 (on A100, add max_num_batched_tokens=16384 and
# max_num_seqs=1024 to the LLM kwargs to match H100's offline defaults)
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python repro_gemma2.py
```

No accuracy evaluation was run: when the new floor applies, every sequence in the batch fits inside the window, so the attention result is mathematically the same and only the kernel's accumulation order changes.

<details>
<summary>FA3 kernel trace of the updated test's workload (target 0, 233 prompt tokens; the other 3 targets match)</summary>

FULL decode graphs are captured with `max_seqlen_k=8192` and window `(4095, 0)`, so FA3 keeps the window there: local kernel, kBlockN=64.

```text
Without fix
  alone  : prefill eager/k=233/causal/N=80  decode FULL/k=8192/local/N=64, ...
  batched: prefill eager/k=233/causal/N=80  decode eager/k=278/causal/N=80, eager/k=360/causal/N=80, eager/k=393/causal/N=80, ...
  decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched: all 15

With fix
  alone  : prefill eager/k=4097/local/N=64  decode FULL/k=8192/local/N=64, ...
  batched: prefill eager/k=4097/local/N=64  decode eager/k=4097/local/N=64, ...
  decode steps whose FA3 kernel differs alone vs batched: none
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** FA3 picks its kernel on the host from `max_seqlen_k`:

- It drops a left window that covers the longest sequence ([`hopper/flash_api.cpp#L865`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/b273a02621d3c94bc747df67204f591b67f38fae/hopper/flash_api.cpp#L865): `if (window_size_left >= seqlen_k - 1) window_size_left = -1;`), which turns local attention off.
- For head dim 256 the KV tile is `is_local ? 64 : 80` ([`hopper/tile_size.h#L51`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/b273a02621d3c94bc747df67204f591b67f38fae/hopper/tile_size.h#L51)). Once the KV spans more than one tile, a different tile changes the online-softmax accumulation order, and with it the output bits.

vLLM passes the batch's real maximum as `max_seqlen_k` in eager steps, but `max_model_len` when capturing FULL CUDA graphs (`for_cudagraph_capture` in MRV1 `gpu_model_runner.py` and MRV2 `model_states/default.py`). With `max_model_len` above the window (8192 vs 4096 in the issue), uniform-decode steps replay graphs that keep the window. Mixed prefill/decode steps run attention eagerly and drop it, unless some sequence in the batch is longer than the window. Without CUDA graphs the same flip happens whenever a batch contains a sequence longer than the window. This matches the issue's results, which were invariant in four cases: with `max_model_len=4096`, with CUDA graphs off and only short prompts, with TRITON_ATTN, and with the sliding window disabled.

**Fix.** Under batch invariance, raise `max_seqlen_k` to at least `window_left + 2` for windowed layers. FA then keeps the window and uses the local kernel in every step, matching the captured graphs. FA2's drop rule (`window_size_left >= max_seqlen_k`) is covered by the same floor.

**Why it is safe.** FA uses `max_seqlen_k` only for host-side decisions (window drop, tile and scheduling heuristics, declared page-table extent). Per-request lengths come from `seqused_k`, which is how captured graphs already run with `max_model_len`. Two existing tests run below the window (`max_model_len` 2048 and 4096, so the floor exceeds `max_model_len`), and both pass on FA2. The added code only compares Python ints, so it adds no GPU sync.

**Not a duplicate.**

- No open PR references #65587.
- #48694 (open, for #47069) routes all regular Hopper attention to FA2 under batch invariance. That would also hide this bug, but it gives up FA3 for every model. This change keeps FA3 and fixes the window-specific cause, and the two are independent.
- flash-attention#169 (open) adds an FA3 `batch_invariant` mode that pins the MMA warpgroup, paged-KV TMA, split-KV and decode causal choices. It leaves the window drop alone, so it would not fix this on its own.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- Under batch invariance, head-dim-256 windowed layers on FA3 now always use the 64-wide local tile. That includes `max_model_len` at or below the window, where they previously always used the 80-wide one. Not benchmarked; batch-invariant mode only.
- Head-dim-128 windowed models (e.g. Gemma-2-27B, Granite SWA) get a 128-wide tile from both kernels on vLLM's paged-KV path, which is why they were not affected.
- `_forward_encoder_attention` (encoder-only sliding-window models) drops the window the same way. I left it out because there is no report for it and nothing to test it on here.
- In CI, only the H100 batch invariance job runs this on FA3. B200 and A100 run FA2 under batch invariance, so they pass with or without the fix, and ROCm skips the test.

AI assistance (Claude in Cursor) was used for the investigation, the fix, the test and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

## Overview

- Fixes `:amd: (MI250) V1 Engine` in nightly https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100748 (`assert 10 == 0`). The MI300 V1 Engine step runs the same file. No product code changes.

cd tests && VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest -v -s v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py

commits.pr_title: [Core] Remove Model Runner V1
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Draft / preview.** This PR removes Model Runner V1 (MRV1). MRV2 is already the default. MRV1 was only reached through an explicit `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` or by falling back for features MRV2 lacks. This PR deletes MRV1 together with the code that existed only for it. Features that only worked on MRV1 are dropped rather than ported. Dual Batch Overlap is kept and now runs on MRV2 by default.

The later commits clean up what the removal left behind, one topic per commit, so they are easiest to review individually. They also deprecate `parallel_drafting`: nothing reads it anymore, since DFlash and DSpark always draft in parallel and no other method supports it. Setting it now logs a deprecation warning, and setting it to `True` for any other method still raises.

## Claims

- **Runner deleted:** `gpu_model_runner.py` (7.2K lines), `gpu_input_batch.py`, `gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`, `cpu_model_runner.py`, the KV/EC connector runner mixins, and the V1 `BlockTable`.
- **V1-only code deleted:**
  - The V1 spec-decode proposers (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/{eagle,dflash,draft_model,ngram*,suffix_decoding,custom_class_proposer,...}.py`) and their Triton kernels.
  - The V1 sampler and rejection sampler.
  - The V1 custom logits-processor API (`vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/`). `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor` is now the only interface.
  - `cpu_triton_utils` and the CPU kernel overrides.
- **`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` and `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` removed.** Every V1/V2 branch in config, worker, scheduler, warmups, models and connectors now takes the V2 path. Startup now fails if `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is set to anything but `1`. Setting it to `1` is redundant and logs a warning, so existing recipes keep working.
- **Interfaces simplified now that only one runner reads them:** `CachedRequestData.resumed_req_ids` and `all_token_ids`, `ModelRunnerOutput.req_id_to_index`, `SchedulerOutput.ec_manager_metadata`, `CudagraphDispatcher`, `TopKTopPSampler`, `build_for_drafting` and `set_cudagraph_capturing_enabled` are removed, and `NewRequestData.prefill_token_ids` is now required. Resumed requests always arrive in `scheduled_new_reqs`.
- **Newly deprecated, with a warning and no longer doing what they did:** `capture_torch_profiler` and `enable_layerwise_nvtx_tracing`.
- **Dropped features.** These now raise, or the option is gone:
  - the `custom_class` speculative method
  - `use_heterogeneous_vocab` (TLI)
  - `disable_padded_drafter_batch`
  - `parallel_drafting` outside `dflash`/`dspark` (P-EAGLE, PARD)
  - pipeline parallelism with `external_launcher`
  - pooling tasks outside the MRV2 set
  - `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor` (DeepSeek-OCR)
  - **vLLM on x86 CPU without Triton** (triton-cpu). Non-x86 CPUs (Arm, POWER, s390x) without Triton keep working on MRV2's standalone CPU model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/cpu/standalone_model_runner.py`).
- **DBO:** the env gate that pushed `--enable-dbo` onto MRV1 is removed. Combinations DBO still doesn't support raise an error. `docs/design/dbo.md` now describes the MRV2 implementation.
- **Docs, examples and requirements:** the PARD docs, the V1 logits-processor design doc, and the V1 logits-processor examples are removed, and the suffix decoding docs now describe only the GPU speculator. `arctic-inference` is dropped from the test requirements.

## Validation

- From the first version of the PR, before the rebases: an import smoke test of the touched core modules (config, workers, scheduler, engine, elastic EP, warmups, models) passed. End-to-end with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` on 1x GB200, with and without `ngram` spec decode, gave identical, sensible greedy outputs.
- On the current branch: pre-commit passes over the whole diff, including ruff, mypy and the test-tethering check (the `pip-compile*` hooks were skipped locally).
- Targeted runs on 1x GB200, across recent rebases: `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/config/test_config_utils.py`, `test_engine_metrics` and `test_draft_model_tensor_parallelism` passed, as did the new `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` startup tests, which fail without the change.
- Earlier full CI runs on previous versions of this branch found the failures fixed here, including stale `ignored_factors` entries that broke engine compile with a speculative config. `test_speculative_config_compile_factors` now covers that case, and fails without the fix.
- Tests: tests that only exercised removed V1 code are deleted, and V1/V2 parametrizations now keep only the V2 path. Coverage that would otherwise be lost is ported to MRV2:
  - the M-RoPE prompt-embeds regression test (`tests/v1/worker/test_mrope_prompt_embeds.py`)
  - the deferred SimpleCPUOffload store test
  - the eager fast-prefill-off case of `test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill`
  - the Triton ReplaySSM e2e tests, which run on MRV2 again
- Not run yet on the current branch: full CI (planned), including the Kimi K3.1 code that landed in the last rebase, and model evals.

## Details

Open questions for reviewers:

1. **x86 CPU without Triton.** Non-x86 CPUs without Triton are covered by the standalone CPU model runner, but x86 now requires triton-cpu. Is that acceptable?
2. **Dropped speculative-decoding features** (custom proposer class, TLI, P-EAGLE/PARD). Do we land this before any of them are ported to MRV2, or wait?

Follow-ups not included here:

- Dropping "V2" naming (`GPUModelRunner` lives under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`).

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py fails when AITER is on. The cause is AITER's RMSNorm has different implementation compared with HF version, and the inductor generates different fused kernels when AITER is on. More important, the results are so sensitive to those small diffs is because the ppl calculation is not accurate. Those prompt tokens outside the reference answer --- the system prompt, the question and the chat-template markup --- those tokens are nearly unpredictable, so their log-probs sit in the softmax tail, where tiny numerical differences move them a lot. They made up 20%+ of the scored tokens but about two-thirds of the total loss, and those are just numerical noises. As a fix, I updated the PPL calculation based on only answer tokens, and reference PPL is also updated accordingly.

Also, the other file, test_glm.py, is also updated with the new calculation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Step5][Spec Decode] Skip VllmConfig re-validation for the MTP draft config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix NVIDIA Step5 MTP startup with pipeline parallelism and preserve the target's resolved CUDA graph settings when constructing the draft config view. Reuse the derived-view handling introduced in #58212.

## Claims

- Step5 MTP starts with PP > 1 without validating the `Step5MTP` architecture against the target's pipeline size.
- Constructing the draft view preserves the target's `cudagraph_mode` and `use_breakable_cudagraph` settings.
- The view retains the draft's HF config and the target's shared runtime configs without modifying the original `draft_model_config`.

## Validation

Serving and evaluation used `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview` (FP8) on NVIDIA B300, Model Runner V2, expert parallelism, three speculative tokens, and prefix caching disabled.

| Configuration | Startup | GSM8K accuracy | MTP acceptance rate | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PP2 × TP2, before fix | `NotImplementedError` | — | — | — |
| PP2 × TP2, this PR | OK | 0.931 | 0.765 | 3.294 |
| PP1 × TP4, before fix | OK | 0.929 | 0.766 | 3.297 |
| PP1 × TP4, this PR | OK | 0.929 | 0.764 | 3.292 |

**CUDA graph capture, PP1 × TP4 with MTP:**

| | Before fix | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CUDA graph mode | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` |
| Graph memory | 0.69 GiB | 4.74 GiB |
| KV cache capacity | 983,723 tokens | 925,755 tokens |

The fixed run retains the same graph mode as the deployment without MTP. Restoring piecewise prefill graphs increases graph memory and reduces the space available for KV cache.

**Prompt logprobs, PP1 × TP4:** six fixed prompts, 418 positions, `prompt_logprobs=0`. Each row compares MTP enabled against MTP disabled under the listed graph setting.

| Code / graph setting | Mean absolute logprob difference | Maximum absolute logprob difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| This PR / default | 0 | 0 |
| This PR / `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 0 | 0 |
| Before fix / default | 0.048 | 4.04 |
| Before fix / `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | 0 | 0 |

**Serving throughput, PP1 × TP4:** random 2,048-token inputs and 256-token outputs, one run per configuration.

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s, before → after | TTFT, before → after | TPOT, before → after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 256 | 1008.5 → 1064.3 | 1183 → 1146 ms | 57.6 → 54.6 ms |
| 8 | 64 | 239.0 → 251.7 | 327 → 241 ms | 31.4 → 30.1 ms |

**Regression tests:** `test_mtp_config_view` builds real Step5 engine configs at PP1 and PP2 using config downloads and `load_format="dummy"`, then constructs the MTP view. It checks draft HF-config identity, shared parallel-config identity, preservation of the original draft config's flag, and unchanged target graph settings.

| Test | Before fix | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_mtp_config_view[1]` | Graph-mode assertion fails | Passed |
| `test_mtp_config_view[2]` | PP validation raises `NotImplementedError` | Passed |
| Entire `tests/models/step5` suite | — | 15 passed, 17 ROCm-only tests skipped |

The existing `:nvidia: (H200) Step5` CI step selects the new test through `pytest -v -s models/step5`. Full-checkpoint serving, GSM8K, logprob, and throughput measurements above ran on B300 outside CI.

<details>
<summary>Regression output</summary>

```text
# Before fix
FAILED models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[1] - AssertionError: assert <CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY: (2, 0)> == <CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE: (2, 1)>
FAILED models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[2] - NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model. ...

# This PR
models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[1] PASSED
models/step5/test_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_config_view[2] PASSED
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Run from the repository root with the vLLM environment activated:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2
```

For PP1 × TP4, use `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1`. For the no-MTP comparison, omit `--speculative-config`. Repeat the logprob comparisons with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` set on both server runs.

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --ignore-eos

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/models/step5/test_mtp_config.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/models/step5
```

The logprob comparison uses `/v1/completions` with identical prompts, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`, and `prompt_logprobs=0`.

</details>

## Details

`_get_mtp_vllm_config()` replaces the target's `model_config` with the draft's config while retaining the target's parallel, cache, and compilation config objects. Since `replace()` reconstructs the dataclass, it re-enters `VllmConfig.__post_init__` with the draft architecture and the target's deployment settings.

This causes two failures:

1. At PP > 1, `verify_with_parallel_config()` rejects `Step5MTP`, even though the MTP head runs entirely on the last stage.
2. With default CUDA graph settings, `Step5MTP` is absent from the breakable-graph default list. Initialization disables breakable graphs and downgrades the shared graph mode from `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, changing the target's configuration after its model has been constructed.

The helper now shallow-copies the initialized draft `ModelConfig`, marks the copy with `is_submodel_config=True`, and creates the view through the existing early-return path. The draft retains its HF config objects, and the runtime configs retain their resolved values. The docstring and early-return comment now describe both submodule and draft views.

#58212 introduced this mechanism for `with_hf_config()` views. #56936 addresses the same reinitialization pattern in the Gemma4 speculator. Open-PR searches found no other change fixing the NVIDIA Step5 MTP config view.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Use promised max_query_len for encoder-only FULL CUDA graphs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With the V2 model runner, models whose attention is encoder-only (non-causal, no KV cache) produce wrong outputs when they
are served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL`.

A FULL CUDA graph for mixed batches is captured on a dummy batch that spreads its tokens over many requests (down to one
token each), but it may later replay a batch with one long prompt. `DefaultModelState` already builds the captured
attention metadata from the batch's promised `max_query_len` for this reason. `EncoderOnlyModelState` instead used the
dummy batch's actual largest query length, so the encoder attention kernels in the graph kept a very short
`max_seqlen_q` / `max_seqlen_k`. Prompts that replay such a graph are then computed incorrectly. There is no error.

The fix applies the same rule as `DefaultModelState`: use `input_batch.max_query_len` when the batch sets it, and fall
back to the largest scheduled query length otherwise.

```python
max_query_len = input_batch.max_query_len
if max_query_len is None:
    max_query_len = int(input_batch.num_scheduled_tokens.max())
```

One file changed (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py`), plus a regression test.

## Claims

- Encoder-only models served with `cudagraph_mode=FULL` give the same outputs as eager execution.
- No change for `PIECEWISE` or `NONE`, for decoder models, or for batches without FULL graphs.
- With the fix, FULL graphs are a correct option for these models: slightly faster single-request reads than PIECEWISE,
  about equal under load (table below).

## Validation

| test | hardware | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_only_full_cudagraph.py`: `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` with `is_causal=False`, FP32, prompts of 23 / 150 / 600 / 1000 tokens one at a time; FULL (capture to 1024) vs eager, last-position logprobs, atol = rtol = 1e-4 | L40S | **fails** (max abs difference 0.034) | passes |
| 8B non-causal decoder fine-tune, FP8, accuracy eval of 13,904 requests, FULL graphs (capture to 8192) vs PIECEWISE | GB200 | 1.5-2 points lower than PIECEWISE (wrong reads) | **identical to PIECEWISE**, two full repeats on each of three configurations (capture to 8192, capture to 2048, 0.6 memory utilization) |
| same eval | L40S | pending | pending |
| ruff check / format | — | | clean |

## Benchmark

NVIDIA GB200 (one GPU), 8B non-causal decoder fine-tune, FP8, `max_cudagraph_capture_size=8192`, one exclusive node,
each configuration measured alone.

| | FULL, this PR | PIECEWISE |
|---|---|---|
| 512-token read, concurrency 1, p50 / p95 | 13.4 / 14.8 ms | 14.0 / 16.5 ms |
| mixed prompts (~1.7k tokens), concurrency 1, requests/s | 35.3 | 32.7 |
| same, concurrency 16, requests/s | 41.8 | 42.8 |
| same, concurrency 64, requests/s | 41.1 | 42.3 |

The main point of the PR is correctness: on main, FULL looks faster (12.6 ms for the same 512-token read) only because
it computes the wrong attention.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Cache only a ROCm stack the PR's CI pushed itself
commits.pr_body:
- `build.sh`: records the stack pair for `/ci rocm cache` under `rocm-rocm-stack-built` only when the build pushed it, not when it reused an existing tag
- `run_ci_command.py`: `/ci rocm cache` copies from the latest build of the PR that recorded it, at any commit, matched by the build's pull request rather than its `github-pr-number` metadata, and names that commit in its reply
- `test_rocm_build.py`, `test_run_ci_command.py`

Follow-up to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65276, which caches the stack image a PR's CI records. A PR build reuses `rocm/vllm-dev:pr<N>-stack-rocm-<key>` if that tag exists. The key is a hash of public files and every PR's CI can push to `rocm/vllm-dev`, so another PR's CI could plant an image under that tag before this PR's CI runs; the PR's CI would record the planted digest, and `/ci rocm cache` would copy it into `rocm/vllm-ci`. The lookup could also be fooled by `github-pr-number`, which any job of any build can set. Now only a stack the PR's own build pushed can be cached; when CI reused one instead, the bot refuses and points to `/ci rocm nocache`. This does not cover the PR's own code, which a maintainer still vouches for, or the `rocm/vllm-ci` push credentials on `amd-cpu`, which PR builds can reach and need a separate fix. `test_run_ci_command.py` (67) and `test_rocm_build.py` (44) pass, and both fail if either check is reverted.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Every engine core and worker process imports `vllm.v1.structured_output` (through `vllm.v1.request`). It imported `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` at module level only for two `isinstance` checks, and that import pulls in `vllm.parser` and with it `openai`, `fastapi`, `starlette` and the `vllm.entrypoints` protocol modules. This is the "EngineCore imports fastapi and the openai protocol types through v1.request → structured_output → parser → entrypoints.*.protocol" item in #59433, and a follow-up to #65423. This PR gives `ReasoningParser` default end-token members and checks those instead, so `vllm.parser` isn't needed there.

## Claims

- After `import vllm.v1.engine.core`, `openai`, `fastapi`, `starlette`, `vllm.entrypoints` and `vllm.parser` modules are no longer loaded, and the import is ~0.7 s faster per process on a B300 (numbers below). The same holds for `vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker` and `vllm.v1.executor.multiproc_executor`.
- Behavior is unchanged: only `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` overrides the new defaults, so other parsers see empty end-token sets, as they effectively did before.
- Scope: this is import-time. When `--reasoning-parser` is set, `StructuredOutputManager.__init__` still loads the parser (and, for non-engine parsers, the protocol modules) at engine start. So the runtime saving applies to engines without a reasoning parser.

## Validation

```bash
python3 tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/reasoning/ tests/parser/
```

```text
# main
  File "vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py", line 14, in <module>
  File "vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py", line 10, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai.types'; 'openai' is not a package
exit 1

# this PR
exit 0
```

`import vllm.v1.engine.core`, 10 fresh processes each:

| | median | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| B300, main | 6.14 s | 6.04 s | 6.23 s |
| B300, this PR | 5.40 s | 5.38 s | 5.52 s |
| macOS CPU, main | 6.17 s | 5.88 s | 8.21 s |
| macOS CPU, this PR | 5.48 s | 5.22 s | 5.72 s |

Modules loaded after that import:

| | openai | fastapi | starlette | vllm.entrypoints | vllm.parser | xgrammar | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300, main | 522 | 38 | 21 | 17 | 10 | 25 | 5530 |
| B300, this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 25 | 4855 |
| CPU, main | 522 | 38 | 21 | 17 | 10 | 25 | 4797 |
| CPU, this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 25 | 4122 |

B300 is vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a` with #65423 and this PR applied (the touched files are identical to this branch's base). CPU is macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `lazy_imports.py` passes on both, and also fails again if the module-level adapter import is put back.

Tests on CPU: 7940 passed on main and with this PR. The same 2 tests fail on both (`test_backend_xgrammar.py::TestXgrammarBackend::TestPR58067Regressions::test_disable_any_whitespace_is_{false,true}`, a fixture-discovery error unrelated to this change). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run --files` (including mypy) pass on the changed files.

## Details

- `ReasoningParser` gets `reasoning_end_token_ids` and `implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids` (properties returning an empty `frozenset()`, matching the adapter's property overrides) and `find_reasoning_end` returning `None`. The structured output manager now checks `reasoner.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids` (masked ids) and `reasoner.reasoning_end_token_ids` (constraint bounds) directly. The implicit check stays first, so the grammar assert still only runs for parsers with implicit end tokens. `MockReasoner` in the manager tests now inherits `ReasoningParser`. The new members are read-only properties so the adapter's overrides type-check; an out-of-tree subclass that assigns `self.reasoning_end_token_ids = ...` would now fail (none in-tree).
- `xgrammar` stays on the startup path. `XgrammarGrammar` in `backend_xgrammar.py` is a dataclass whose field annotations (`xgr.GrammarMatcher`, `xgr.CompiledGrammar`) are evaluated at class creation, which resolves the `xgr` lazy loader. So this PR doesn't move any import to the first request.
- `lazy_imports.py` now blocks `openai`, `fastapi` and `starlette`, and imports `vllm.v1.structured_output`. `vllm.v1.engine.core` can't be used there yet because `vllm.utils.deep_gemm` still imports `torch._inductor.async_compile` (#65590).
- CI: `lazy_imports.py` currently runs only in the `(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser` job, which is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (#63609). #64414 restores it.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this import. #56239, #57310 and #65590 also edit the end of `lazy_imports.py`, so whichever lands later needs a trivial rebase.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to draft the change, the tests and this description. I reviewed the changes, the measurements and the test results before submitting.
